label: 20-year-old who grew up in a big-city neighbourhood
summary: Grew up in the urban core of a major city such as Los Angeles, Chicago, New York, or Miami, and is now working, studying locally, or both. Has no tie to Yale and would wear its apparel as style, not affiliation. Fluent in music, streetwear, and social video, and quick to notice when a brand borrows that culture without earning it.
life_stage: 20, early in work or college, living in their home city
relationship_to_yale: None directly; knows Yale as a famous and exclusive university
yale_traditions_valued: The name as a recognised symbol of prestige
Classic collegiate lettering as a fashion look
Ivy League standing, viewed with both interest and scepticism
yale_modern_values: Whether elite universities are really open to people from neighbourhoods like theirs
Representation: seeing people who look and dress like them treated with respect
Honesty about privilege rather than pretending it is not there
personal_values: Authenticity and being true to where they come from
motivations: Wearing what artists, athletes, and people they respect are wearing
A sense of aspiration, on their own terms
purchase_occasions: Seeing a piece in a video or on someone whose style they rate
A new release or limited run
decision_drivers: Fit, weight, and how the garment looks worn
Credibility: who is wearing it and whether the brand feels real
Price against the streetwear and sportswear brands they already buy
A link that goes straight to the product
apparel_preferences: Bold collegiate lettering in navy, black, or gray
Pieces that work with sneakers and everyday streetwear
media_habits: TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, with sound on
Watches music videos and creators closely and shares what stands out
Scrolls past anything that looks like a conventional advert
cultural_references: Hip-hop past and present, including well-known music videos
tone_that_resonates: Led by music and visuals rather than a sales pitch
Made with the culture, not about it
call_to_action_needs: Where to buy, as a direct link or handle
turn_offs: Awkward imitation of music videos or street style
No way to find or buy the item shown
appropriateness_concerns: An elite institution using urban settings or hip-hop imagery as a costume
City life shown as a caricature, or people used as background props
Mocking the artists or communities a style comes from
